column1: # What each card can do per arithmetic lane.
# How the rows are used: lanes/gen-tables.cmake compiles them in when CMake configures (lanes-table.h, with lanes.tsv).
# ggml_metal_lane_ok_mask (lanes/select.cpp) turns the rows of one card into the set of lanes it may use: a lane counts
# only when reached and correct are both yes. No file is read at run time.
# To add a row: run the lane probe on the card, or cite the document, and write where the cell values come from in source.
# In the three yes | no | unknown columns, unknown reads as no.
#   pci: the card as 0xVVVV:0xDDDD (PCI vendor and device id, lower-case hex). A card with no row can use the base lane of each route only.
#   lane: the capability name a lanes.tsv row asks for in its capability column (for example pk-mul-f16, dot4-i32-i8).
#   in_hardware: the chip has the instruction: yes | no | unknown. For the reader. The selector does not use it.
#   reached: the Metal shader compiler emits the instruction (seen as throughput in the probe): yes | no | unknown.
#   correct: the result equals the CPU reference: yes | no | unknown.
#   ratio: throughput against the fp32 lane on that card, or - when not timed. For the reader.
#   source: where the cells come from: the probe and its date, or the document. Free text, no tab.
